text:
Maya: Hey, I'm trying to pick a new credit card. You use the one with travel points, right?
Ben: Yeah. Two points per dollar on travel and dining, one on everything else. Annual fee is ninety-five.
Maya: Is it worth it?
Ben: For me, yes. I fly maybe six times a year. But if you don't travel much, a flat two percent cashback card with no annual fee is simpler.
Maya: I spend about two thousand a month, mostly groceries and gas. Would the points card help?
Ben: Not really. Look for a card with five percent on groceries and gas rotating categories. Some have a cap, though, like fifteen hundred a quarter.
Maya: Oh, yeah, I saw those. I get confused with the activation every quarter.
Ben: That's the annoying part. Honestly, a flat two percent is about forty bucks a month back for you, and zero thinking.
Maya: Okay. What about the foreign transaction fee? I'm going to Lisbon in the summer.
Ben: Pick one with no foreign fee. Most travel cards don't charge it, but regular cashback ones usually add three percent.
Maya: Good point. I'll look for both. Thanks, Ben.
Ben: Sure. And always pay the full balance, otherwise the interest kills all the rewards.

metadata.note: friend call comparing credit cards: cashback vs travel rewards
